title: Playing Bach at Hamilton and her poor retention of music
summary: Rowe recalls her being unable to speak after a Bach piece at Hamilton; she worries she remembers little of the music she hears.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It makes me think of the anecdote you told me about going to Hamilton College and participating in what you think was a Bach piece and that you said it affected you so much that you couldn’t even speak.
I really had trouble talking for a couple of days.
I think that says a lot about your level of empathy with music I guess.

I hope so. I criticize myself because I have a terrible — you know most of my friends who are musicians, everyone in Italy but also most of my friends here, you know remember every album they’ve listened to, the name, the cuts, who played on them, they’ve got it all catalogued, you know, what they read, the books they read. Everything goes in my mind and out, I have so little retention. I think does this mean I’m too superficial about music, but it’s just — I hope that what you’re saying is the greater truth.
